# @admiral-ds/react-ui

React component library based on the Admiral 2.1 design system

## Contents

- [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/AdmiralDS/react-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Setup](#setup)

## Installation

@admiral-ds/react-ui requires dependencies:

1. `styled-components > 5.1.0`
2. `react > 16.0.0`
3. `react-dom > 16.0.0`

   You can use a ready-made template with the configured library [https://github.com/AdmiralDS/web-app-vite-admiral](https://github.com/AdmiralDS/web-app-vite-admiral)
   or create a project from scratch and install the library:

```shell
$ npm create vite@latest my-web-app -- --template react-ts
$ cd my-web-app
$ npm install
$ npm i @admiral-ds/react-ui
$ npm run dev
```

## Setup

For @admiral-ds/react-ui to work properly, you need to use `<ThemeProvider>`, `<FontsVTBGroup />` and `<DropdownProvider>`, and it is **recommended** to connect them at the root of the project:

main.tsx

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import { ThemeProvider } from 'styled-components';
import { LIGHT_THEME, FontsVTBGroup, DropdownProvider } from '@admiral-ds/react-ui';
import…
```

CXH0920/mjs_agent_project.body:
# Legendary General Kill Agent

A multimodal desktop application based on **OCR + RAG** with a focus on the mobile game 'Legendary General Kill'. The project primarily explores:

- **Multimodal screen recognition**: Template matching pre-filtering + RapidOCR recognition + Chinese character feature library name correction
- **RAG corpus hierarchical architecture**: ODS/DWD/mart three-tier data warehouse stratification, corpus task single source of truth scheduling and version stamps
- **Multi-vendor LLM integration**: API (multi-vendor profile) + browser automation dual backend, RAG corpus-enhanced generation
- **Desktop application engineering**: PySide6 + PyInstaller dual-mode packaging, CI integration and release smoke testing pipeline

> ⚠️ **Usage Notice**
>
> This project is a **personal technical exploration and portfolio demonstration** project with no affiliation with the operator of the 'Legendary General Kill' game, intended solely for personal learning, research, and technical exchange:
>
> 1. Prohibition on commercial use;
> 2. Prohibition on cheat modification (auto-clicking, process injection, memory modification, hooking, anti-cheat bypass);
> 3. Collected data is limited to local use only, prohibition on secondary distribution;
> 4. General avatar images are downloaded from the official website by default for local display, AI-generated content is for reference only, please self-evaluate legal risks.
>
> See [LICENSE](https://github.com/CXH0920/mjs_agent_project/blob/HEAD/LICENSE) (supplementary terms of use) and [TERMS.md](https://github.com/CXH0920/mjs_agent_project/blob/HEAD/TERMS.md) for details. The desktop application will display a disclaimer upon first launch or after terms update, and can proceed after confirmation.

---

## Technical Highlights

1. **Multimodal screen recognition** — OpenCV template matching as pre-filtering (<50ms), RapidOCR full-screen recognition is executed only on match; Chinese character feature library based on Sijiao code, radicals, stroke count, and pinyin for OCR name correction; polling throughout memory processing without disk writes, multiple modules share a single screenshot.
2. **RAG corpus hierarchical architecture** — ODS (official website raw JSON / official rankings) → DWD (10 types of corpus task processing, `task_defs.py` single source of truth) → mart (generate injection corpus and retrieval indexes) three-tier data warehouse stratification; corpus chunks carry `as_of`/`is_current` version stamps, retrieval layer defaults to calling only current versions, outdated chunks carry failure reasons.
3. **Multi-vendor LLM integration** — API mode (httpx + multi-vendor profile: deepseek / openai / ollama / openai-compatible) and browser automation mode (Playwright + Edge) dual backend, consistent output format; 429 rate limit backoff, token split statistics and cost estimation.
4. **Testing and delivery engineering** — 116 test modules / 1491 test functions; CI uses pytest-xdist for parallel execution + 60…

Nianjiujiang/pdx-map-editor.body:
# Map Editor (CK3 / EU4 / HOI4 / Victoria 3 / EU5)

> Author: **永夜廿九** (same name on Bilibili)

A small tool in the browser for coloring game maps, changing colors, and exporting. Click any region you want to modify, and when done you can export to an image or save the coloring to a file to continue next time.

Supports 5 games, 7 maps:

- **Crusader Kings 3** (CK3)
- **Europa Universalis IV** (EU4)
- **Hearts of Iron IV** (HOI4) — Vanilla + Modified Borders
- **Victoria 3** (Victoria 3)
- **Europa Universalis V** (EU5) — Vanilla + Original Size (Chunked Loading)

---

## 1. Getting Started

**This tool is a single file**: `pdx-map-editor.html` (approximately 35 MB, with data for all 7 maps baked in). Get it, **double-click** it, and open it in a browser (Chrome / Edge / Firefox all work). The first screen lets you **select a map** and click to enter.

Ways to get it (choose one):

- **Easiest**: Go to [Releases](https://github.com/Nianjiujiang/pdx-map-editor/blob/HEAD/../../releases) and download this one file (that's all that's there);
- **In the repository**: Open `pdx-map-editor.html` in the root directory, click "Download raw file" in the top right; if you've already cloned the repository, it's in the root directory, just double-click it.

No installation needed, no internet required, no need to run a server. Copy it to another computer (USB drive, cloud storage) and it works just the same.

> Those who want to rebuild the data or modify the code themselves, see [`docs/构建与开发说明.md`](https://github.com/Nianjiujiang/pdx-map-editor/blob/HEAD/docs/构建与开发说明.md).

## 2. Interface Layout

- **Top bar**: On the left "**View**" is a row of level buttons (click to switch to that level); in the middle "**Tools**"; on the right is "Settings" "Export ▾" "↶ ↷ Clear";
- **Left sidebar**, from top to bottom: **Display** (color / border / name toggle for each level), **Current color** (the color in use + marker name), **Hovered province** (which province the mouse is pointing at), **Find** (search box), **Palette** (all used colors are saved, click to use again);
- **Center**: Map. Hold and drag to pan, scroll wheel to zoom.

### View and "Granularity"

Level buttons are the "View": switch to a level and the map displays that level's coloring and borders.

Unified authentication · Account pool rotation · Circuit breaking and cooldown · Session affinity · Scheduled check-in and renewal · Management console

## What is this

**multi2api is a multi-upstream aggregation reverse proxy gateway**: it combines multiple upstream accounts into a single OpenAI-compatible `base_url` + `api_key`. Your application only needs to understand the OpenAI protocol, and the gateway handles account selection, quotas, check-ins, renewals, cooldown, and troubleshooting behind the scenes.

```
Your application ──► multi2api ──┬──► WorkBuddy          Tencent CodeBuddy Desktop (default upstream)
                         ├──► WorkBuddy AI       Overseas version (www.workbuddy.ai)
                         ├──► CodeArts           Huawei Cloud CodeArts
                         ├──► Loomy              iFLYTEK Loomy Desktop
                         ├──► Cline              Cline Desktop
                         ├──► TRAE               ByteDance TRAE
                         ├──► Raccoon Work       SenseTime Xiaohuan
                         ├──► LobsterAI          Youdao Lobster
                         ├──► Qoder              Alibaba Qoder
                         ├──► Qoder (China version)
                         └──► ZCode              Z.ai / Zhipu GLM Coding Plan
```

> ⚠ **It is no longer WorkBuddy-specific only**. Architecturally, 'adding one upstream = adding one directory + implementing one set of interfaces + adding one configuration section, **zero changes to core**'—this is the hardest criterion for this project, enforced by the **executable assertions** in `internal/gateway/arch_test.go` (not a convention):
>
> - The core package must not depend on any specific upstream
> - Upstreams must not depend on each other
> - Adding a new upstream requires only adding one line `registry.Register(...)` in `cmd/server/main.go`
>
> During the expansion from 4 to 10 upstreams, the core package **was not changed by a single line** — this criterion is proven in practice, not just rhetoric.

Unson-LLC/brainbase.body:
# Brainbase

## Don't limit your judgment power to just one person.

Brainbase turns your purpose, priorities, judgment criteria, and past decisions into a local judgment OS that multiple AIs can use. Codex and Claude Code can think deeply from the same judgment axis and advance research, design, writing, and development.

> **Use your smart self as both a thinking partner and an execution team.**

Humans decide the purpose, judgment criteria, and scope of work to delegate. AI references these to explore, provide counter-evidence, and advances work within the permitted scope.

## Why It's Needed

At companies, even when documents and meeting notes remain, the following tend to remain in people's heads:

- Why this customer was prioritized
- Why profitable proposals were rejected
- What we protect by choosing that policy
- How much can be delegated to AI or other staff members
- What should be changed after seeing the results of execution

In this state, the same explanation is needed for AI every time, judgment quality drops when staff changes, and important decisions keep being returned to management.

Brainbase preserves not only "what was decided" but also **for whom, what was prioritized, what was protected, and on what basis the decision was made**.

## Concrete Example

Suppose the company policy was "not to increase one-off contracts, but to select projects that become reusable assets."

A typical AI might recommend taking orders based only on revenue or profit margins. An AI referencing Brainbase can confirm management workload, reusability, existing policies, and customer relationships, and make decisions like this:

> While short-term revenue can be obtained, it increases management's individual workload and leaves no reusable assets, so it doesn't align with the current policy. It could become a candidate for orders if implementation procedures are standardized so that other staff members can also execute them.

Brainbase's value is not in storing large amounts of information. It's about **passing on to the next person and AI why that person or company would make that judgment**.

## Current OSS Version

This repository provides Brainbase's common Judgment DAG infrastructure and the first entry point, a locally-prioritized Personal Onboarding Kit.

The main features currently available are as follows:

- Save yourself, projects, stakeholders, judgment criteria, and decisions to local SSOT
- Reference context from Codex, Claude Code, CodeCode via MCP
- Connect people, organizations, projects, and judgments with canonical IDs using Graph v2 and Ontology 2.0.0
- Connect requests to the correct context with `resolve_entity`, `get_context`, `search`
- Type-check Judgment DAG and execute with a local deterministic runner…

# Dogi — AI-driven Operations Workbench

Electron + React desktop R&D and DevOps tool: consolidates 'connecting to machines → working → recording → calling APIs → letting AI handle it' all in one app. Activity bar on the left, VS Code-style split-screen tabbed groups on the right; built-in terminal / SSH / remote desktop / SFTP / server monitoring / API debugging / notes / scripts / plugin host, and an AI Agent capable of reading/writing files, executing commands, and invoking skills.

## Features

### Terminal and Hosts

- **Local Terminal**: `node-pty`, automatically detects PowerShell / pwsh / CMD / Git Bash / WSL / bash / zsh / fish, can specify default shell
- **SSH**: `ssh2`, password or private key authentication, handshake progress pushed in real-time, automatic reconnection on failure, keepalive, multiple sessions
- **Windows Servers**: direct connection to system built-in OpenSSH; after session is ready, automatically detects host platform (Linux / Windows), AI provides corresponding syntax command hints per platform; per-host terminal encoding (UTF-8 / GBK, switch to GBK when Chinese servers show garbled text)
- **Multi-tab + Split**: `@xterm/xterm` v6 (DOM rendering), VS Code-style panel tree — split up/down/left/right, drag to adjust ratios, move tabs across groups
- **zmodem**: directly use `sz` / `rz` in terminal to transfer files (use system dialog to select/save files)
- **Server Monitoring**: collect via SSH from `/proc` + `df`, real-time display of CPU / memory / load / network speed / disk / uptime, configurable interval; currently supports Linux only — non-Linux hosts explicitly show "monitoring not supported" indicator instead of silently disappearing monitoring bar
- **SFTP File Manager**: browse, upload, download (including recursive directories), remote copy / move, rename / delete / create directory; transfer progress aggregated to status bar transfer tray, can cancel anytime
- **Remote Desktop (RDP)**: one of three host types (SSH / remote desktop / local terminal, can change after creation); embedded WASM client (`ironrdp-wasm`) renders to canvas, separate tab; main process local WebSocket bridge connects directly to host configured address and port (doesn't call mstsc), supports scaling / keyboard/mouse / Ctrl+Alt+Del; credentials read from host config (`safeStorage` encrypted), can also check save to config when connecting
- Session output ring buffer (256KB / session), for AI and debugging to read
- Terminal color schemes (follow theme / dark / light / Solarized Dark / Dracula / Nord), font size scaling, copy on select, right-click paste, command prediction

---

⚠️ Cautions

**Please confirm the following before using this API.**

- **It is unofficial.** It has no relation to the official BOATRACE website or related organizations.
- **It is not real-time.** Due to periodic updates at approximately 3-minute intervals via GitHub Actions, there may be a delay of several minutes before the latest information is reflected.
- **Accuracy and completeness are not guaranteed.** Due to the nature of collection and conversion, there may be missing or incorrect data.
- **If you need official information, please always check the official BOATRACE website.**
- **Use at your own risk.**

---

📝 Overview

This API allows you to retrieve boat racing (speedboat racing) data. The data is published on GitHub Pages and provided in JSON format.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Supported venues | All 24 venues nationwide (data for one day contains information for all venues) |
| Available data | Starter list, last-minute information, results |

---

🌐 Endpoints

Supported period: **From January 1, 2026 onwards**

```bash
https://boatraceopenapi.github.io/api/v1/YYYY/YYYYMMDD.json
```

- `YYYY` → Year
- `YYYYMMDD` → Year month day
- Dates are based on Japan Standard Time (JST / UTC+9)

> If you specify a date for which data does not exist (outside the supported period, future dates, etc.), GitHub Pages will return HTTP 404 according to its specifications.

---

📦 Response Specification

For details on the JSON structure of the response and each field, refer to the schema documentation.

→ [docs/v1/schema.md](https://github.com/boatraceopenapi/api/blob/HEAD/docs/v1/schema.md)

luxxuria/harvester.body:
## CDN Mirrors

If `github` is unreachable or blocked in your country, you can access any file by replacing the domain in the URL using the templates below:

* **jsDelivr:** `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/luxxuria/harvester@main/FILENAME.txt`
* **GitHack:** `https://raw.githack.com/luxxuria/harvester/main/FILENAME.txt`

*Replace `FILENAME.txt` with: `ping_tested.txt`, `speed_tested.txt`, or `non_ru.txt`.*

# Harvester

All the neural code was completely rewritten by hand, with the goal of learning something and solving current problems.
The script now uses less CPU time due to reducing the spawning of xray cores and other optimizations, and unnecessary buffers and memory-consuming vectors have been removed.
The pipeline became more linear, the code more readable, and more context for errors has been added. In the future, possibly xray configs will be updated via grpc instead of restarts.

## Proxy Files

metasequoiaime/msime.body:
# Metasequoia Input Method

Metasequoia Input Method (MSIME) is a multi-platform Chinese input method for Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, and HarmonyOS. Each of the six platforms has its own native input method host, all connecting to the same shared input runtime and the same React settings interface; the React management interface calls a standard Rust business library through Tauri; the input algorithm is provided by msime-engine.

Project homepage: [msime.app](https://msime.app/) · [GitHub repository](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime) · [Contributors](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime/graphs/contributors) · [Issue feedback](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime/issues) · [Code signing policy](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime-windows/blob/develop/docs/code-signing-policy.md)

## Star History

> **About the Name**: MSIME is short for Metasequoia IME (Metasequoia Input Method), unrelated to Microsoft IME and has no association with Microsoft. The `msime` in code, package names, and repository names all refer to this meaning. The `shuangpin_profile: microsoft` in settings is the "Microsoft Shuangpin" scheme, one of four key layout schemes alongside Xiaohao, Ziran, and Shoudao, available for users accustomed to this layout, and similarly does not represent any association.

**An input method can see everything you type, so this question should have an answer you can verify line by line: [What data leaves the device](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime/blob/HEAD/PRIVACY.md).** Short version: Under the default configuration of a fresh installation, no feature will send your input content off the device; Cloud Prediction (sending the pinyin being composed to Google Input Tools) requires you to enable it on first prompt or in settings, and all other network functions require you to fill in credentials or select a service before they work. There is also a separate anonymous usage statistic that does not carry input content: all six platforms send daily active, session, and crash records (error summary and call stack with directories removed) to `api.msime.app`, enabled by default, and can be disabled in the "Anonymous usage statistics" section of settings—the fields, platform-specific differences, and storage locations are listed line by line in [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/metasequoiaime/msime/blob/HEAD/PRIVACY.md#使用统计与崩溃上报默认开启可关闭). The repository does not integrate any third-party analytics or crash reporting SDKs.

trtyr/engram.body:
# 🧠 Engram ### Turn AI's memory into distillable, retrievable, auditable, forgettable assets **Single-user AI long-term memory platform · Rust single binary · Ten-domain MCP progressive discovery · Wiki single database · Fully traceable throughout** > **en·gram**（/ˈenɡræm/）*n.* In neuroscience, a "memory trace" — the physical imprint left by memory in the brain. > > **AI's memory should not evaporate with the conversation.** --- ## 💥 What problems does it solve Large language models' memory lives within a single session: close the window, and everything—who the user is, where the project stands, what pitfalls were encountered last time—resets to zero. Stuffing the model with a "notepad" doesn't solve the problem, because **memory quality depends on memory governance**: - Is what you put in trustworthy? — **Every layer must be able to replay where it came from and how it came about** - What if it remembers wrong? — **Error correction follows a replacement chain, not overwriting** - Can it truly forget what you don't want it to remember? — **Forgetting is a first-class citizen, not an UPDATE statement** Engram is a "platform as tool": the platform exposes MCP and HTTP APIs outward, AI (or humans) manipulate with keys; humans govern and browse through a Web console. The core idea in one sentence— > ## Trust comes from traceability 🔍 ## 🖼️ Interface overview **Overview**—the four layers of the memory pipeline (session → atom → scenario → profile) at a glance: | User Memory | Work Ticket | |:---:|:---:| | | | | **Code Graph** | **MCP Tool Surface** | | | | > Screenshots are demo data (fictional characters and projects). ## 🪜 Memory distillation ladder Raw conversation text is not memory; memory is distilled. Engram turns "casual chat" into four layers of governable assets: ```mermaid flowchart LR L0["💬 L0 Session
Original conversation"] -->|Distill| L1["⚛️ L1 Atomic facts
Smallest retrievable unit"] L1 -->|Organize| L2["🌫️ L2 Scenario patterns
Accumulation of similar facts"] L2 -->|Accumulate| L3["👤 L3 User profile
For prompt injection"] L3 -.->|Cold-start injection| AI["🤖 Your AI"] L1 -.->|Targeted recall| AI ``` - **Fully traceable throughout**: Each layer of the distillation chain records `prompt_version`, any memory can be traced back and replayed to the prompt version that produced it - **Error correction via distillation**: Write the correct statement as dialogue, distillation automatically generates a replacement chain—never directly rewrite semantic content - **Forgetting is disconnection**: `forget` invalidates sessions, already-distilled products are **cascadingly archived**, retrieval immediately becomes ineffective - **Entity coordinate system**: People / Projects / Topics / Groups / Places, automatically extracted by distillation, horizontally linking all memories ## 🗂️ Ten-domain assets…

zc310/ofd.description: Go toolkit for OFD: convert (OFD⇄PDF/PNG/JPG/SVG/HTML/Markdown, PDF/MD/Office/HTML→OFD), create, validate, analyze, render, and preview in browser/desktop/android.
zc310/ofd.body:
# OFD Go Toolkit

A Go toolkit for parsing, creating, converting, rendering, validating, and analyzing OFD documents.

> Before using this project and its output results, please read the [Disclaimer](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/blob/HEAD/DISCLAIMER.md). This project does not guarantee that parsing, converting, validating, or rendering results of all OFD files are suitable for specific business, legal, or compliance scenarios. If you discover potentially infringing content in the repository, documentation, or examples, please contact the maintainer through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/issues/new).

## Introduction to OFD

OFD (Open Fixed-layout Document) is a commonly used fixed-layout document format in China's electronic document field, primarily used to preserve electronic files with fixed layouts that display consistently across devices. OFD files are typically organized as ZIP containers containing XML documents, page content, text, paths, images, fonts, attachments, and signatures and other resources; pages can contain text, vector graphics, and raster images, and retain corresponding layout and rendering information. The project includes related standard materials from GB/T 33190-2016 "Electronic File Storage and Exchange Format - Fixed-layout Documents" in the [`docs/standards/`](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/blob/HEAD/docs/standards/) directory for format learning and development reference.

OFD is applicable to electronic certificates, electronic invoices, digital archives, official documents, and other fixed-layout files that require long-term preservation or exchange. This project provides parsing, creation, rendering, conversion, validation, analysis, and reading capabilities around OFD documents, supporting output of OFD content in formats such as PDF, single-file HTML, PNG, JPG, multi-page TIFF, SVG, plain text, and Markdown. OFD files generated by different vendors may have extension or compatibility differences; please refer to [`docs/OFD-SUPPORT.md`](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/blob/HEAD/docs/OFD-SUPPORT.md) for specific support scope.
